A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DIP watermark-evasion work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated figures and renumbered appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original evasion experiments on COCO, DiffusionDB, and TreeRing-watermarked images in Tables 1–4, alongside frequency analyses and visual case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original frequency-band measurements, runtime results, and a WIND-inpainting detection experiment in Table 5, Table 7, and Figure 12.

M1.justification: The DIP regression objective, network choice, optimization, and intermediate-image selection remain unchanged. Section 3.3 expands discussion of decoder access and single-shot use without specifying a new evasion procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix F adds a detection scenario involving clean and WIND-inpainting-watermarked COCO images, extending coverage to another watermark-generation condition. The existing COCO, DiffusionDB, and TreeRing evasion coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the corresponding evasion tables is unchanged. Diffuser and VAE receive revised source attribution, while the new runtime comparison uses existing comparators. WIND-inpainting is tested separately and explicitly excluded from the evasion comparison.

E3.justification: v2 adds a separate ten-band frequency analysis using 100 images per watermark method, a single-image timing protocol, and a WIND detection test using 100 clean images and their 100 watermarked counterparts. Existing benchmark sampling, thresholds, quality metrics, and hyperparameter grids remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 5 adds quantitative spectral analysis of watermark-specific resistance, Table 7 examines computational cost, and Figure 12 checks whether WIND detection distances separate clean and watermarked images. These targeted supporting analyses supplement the retained frequency-learning trajectories and visual case studies.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains the same mean and standard-deviation reporting across 100 images. v2 introduces no new repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures; the added averages and histograms report empirical outcomes.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 retain identical results. New Table 5 reports, for example, band-3 FBE of 0.177 for TrustMark versus 0.070 for SSL. Table 7 adds timings of 26.6 seconds for DIP and 290.75 seconds for DiffPure under their listed configurations. Figure 12 adds overlapping WIND detection-distance distributions.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7 and the existing frequency-band-error formulation are retained. The additional frequency measurements and detection experiment introduce no new formal assumptions, theoretical results, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: DIP is a complementary evasion baseline, frequency separation explains its strengths, no evasion method universally dominates, and stronger low-frequency watermark distortions can improve resistance.

C2.justification: v1 treats TrustMark's resistance as surprising and offers a tentative explanation; v2 uses Table 5 to attribute it to lower/mid-frequency distortions. Section 3.3 clarifies decoder-query requirements, Appendix F explains WIND's exclusion, and the new ethical statement adds a specific argument about misuse risk.

D1.justification: v2 documents Windows, an Intel i7-12700K, an RTX 3080, and method-specific configurations for the new timing experiment. It also changes the advertised code repository from HengyueL/DIP_Watermark_Evasion to sun-umn/DIP_Watermark_Evasion_TMLR. Existing network and hyperparameter disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Arabi et al. (2024) and discusses WIND's identification-versus-detection focus. It clarifies the existing distinction from Rishik's visible-watermark inpainting and revises Diffuser/VAE attribution. The Zhao preprint-to-publication update refers to the same work.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main narrative structure remain intact. v2 retitles and expands Section 3.3, revises the TrustMark discussion, adds appendix explanations and two appendix sections, and replaces the acknowledgments with an ethical statement.

P2.justification: v2 adds the frequency and runtime tables and the WIND histogram. The original hyperparameter table becomes Table 6, while Figures 1–11 retain their visual content. Other changes include journal headers, repositioned floats, and placing Figures 10 and 11 together.

improvement.justification: The quantitative frequency analysis strengthens v1's speculative explanation of TrustMark resistance. Runtime documentation, clearer decoder-access discussion, and the WIND detection check also improve practical assessability. These are limited gains with unchanged main benchmark evidence; the single-image timing study under different listed configurations supports only limited efficiency conclusions.
